summary: Shinko Nakai was a scholar in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto Prefectural University (~1962–1966) and served at Bukkyo University (~1975–2014) as a professor emeritus and former university president.

Shinobu Arai Apple specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied under academic adviser Robert Bickner, teacher Mark Csikszentmihalyi in 2000, and doctoral supervisor Charles Hallisey (attested 2003).
Shinobu Yamaguchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She earned her PhD from Nagoya University in 1995 and held a post as professor at Toyo University (attested 2015).

Shinpei Ogura was a linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1906). He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1926–1933) and the University of Tokyo (~1933–1943), where he succeeded Katsuji Fujioka in 1933.

Shinsho Hanayama was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the Fourth Higher School (~1917–1920) and the University of Tokyo (~1920–1923). He held professorships at Toyo University (~1932–1945), Kokugakuin University (~1935–1945), and the University of Tokyo (~1935–1959).

Shintaro Kitano is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kazunobu Matsuda (attested 2005). He was a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2005) and a part-time lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 2015).

Shintei Hinonishi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Shigeru Gorai. He held academic posts at Koyasan University, serving as an assistant professor (attested 1980) and later as a professor (attested 2008).
Shinten Sakai was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Shindo Shiraishi. He held a post at Koyasan University (attested 1959).

Shinya Moriyama specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1996–1998) and the University of Vienna (~2002–2006, Dr.Phil) under Eli Franco, later teaching at Shinshu University (~2010).

Shinya Yasutomi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1963–1967) and Otani University (~1973–1978, PhD 1998). He served as a professor at Otani University (~1985–2010) and director at the Shinshu Otani-ha Institute (~2010–2016).

Shiro Matsumoto is a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, as well as under Yasuaki Nara and Zuiho Yamaguchi. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (1995–2020).

Shivram Dattatray Joshi was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Śaṅkarśāstri Mārulkar, Maheshvarshastri Joshi, and Daniel H. H. Ingalls at Harvard. He held posts at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1959–1987) and Deccan College (~1987–1996).

Shizuka Sasaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University, UC Berkeley, and Bukkyo University under Jikidō Takasaki, and held posts at Hanazono University from 1990, becoming Professor of Indian Buddhism in 2002.
Shizuka Shirakawa was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics. He studied at Ritsumeikan University from ~1939 to 1943 and later held a post there from ~1954 to 1981.

Shlomo Pines was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Heidelberg, Geneva, and Berlin (1926–1934), and later served on the faculties of the University of Paris (1937–1939) and the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (1952–1990).

Shmuel Sambursky was a scholar of philosophy and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Königsberg (~1920–1922) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1922–1924), and held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1928–1970).

Shobha Rani Dash specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She was an open-recruitment researcher at Ryukoku University (2010), a lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012), and a professor at Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
Shodo Fujita is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Ryukoku University under Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 1995–2013).

Shodo Harada is a Buddhist studies and religious studies master who studied at Shofuku-ji and under Mumon Yamada (1962–1982), whom he succeeded. He became abbot of Sōgen-ji in 1982 and founded Tahoma Sōgenji Zen Monastery in 1995.
Shodo Yamagami is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He completed doctoral credits at Kyoto University in 1964 and served as an assistant professor at Kyoto Sangyo University from ~1978 to 2010.
